findings.evidence: In mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Predictable.lean, `predictable` (line 52) takes `[Preorder ι] [OrderBot ι]`. `measurableSet_predictable_singleton_bot_prod`, `measurableSet_predictable_Ioi_prod` and `measurableSet_predictable_Ioc_prod` (lines 59/64/71) take `[LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]`. The only `ℝ≥0`-specific step in this PR is `exists_nat_ge` in the cofinal union (lines 87, 109).
findings.fix: Generalize to `{ι : Type*} [LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι] (ℱ : Filtration ι m)` and use `{⊥}` in place of `{0}`. State `predictable_eq_generateFrom_elementarySets` and the downstream theorems under a cofinal-sequence hypothesis such as `[(atTop : Filter ι).IsCountablyGenerated]` or `∃ u : ℕ → ι, ∀ x, ∃ n, x ≤ u n`, which replaces `exists_nat_ge`. Recover `ℝ≥0` as an instance.
findings.issue: The variables fix `ℱ : Filtration ℝ≥0 m`. Yet `elementarySets`, `mem_elementarySets_iff`, `measurableSet_of_mem_elementarySets` and `isPiSystem_elementarySets` only use `max`/`min`, `ℱ.mono` and the bottom element. Discrete time (`ℕ`) and other index types cannot use them.

findings.evidence: In the proof, `hzero` is used only to produce `hinit` (line 104). The pi-system step at line 143 already handles initial slices through the `Or.inl` case of `elementarySets`.
findings.fix: Prove the general versions first: the hypothesis `∀ u ∈ ℱ.elementarySets, ∫ p in u, f p ∂μ = 0`, and density of the span of indicators of all elementary sets, with no `hzero`. Then derive the current `Ioc`-only statements from them using `hzero`.
findings.issue: `ae_eq_zero_of_setIntegral_Ioc_prod_eq_zero` and `topologicalClosure_span_indicatorConstLp_Ioc_prod` require `hzero`. The general fact needs no such hypothesis: testing against all of `ℱ.elementarySets`, initial slices included, already determines `f`, and the indicators of all elementary sets span a dense subspace for every finite predictable measure. The `hzero` versions are corollaries.

summary: The elementary-set definition and its membership, measurability and pi-system lemmas are fixed to time `ℝ≥0`, although Mathlib states `predictable` and its rectangle lemmas for `[LinearOrder ι] [OrderBot ι]`. The testing and density theorems prove only the `hzero` special case when the general statement over all elementary sets is just as easy to prove.
